Author: Sudhir Agarwal
Bench: Sudhir Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 34
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 1297 of 1991
Revisionist :- Virendra
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- Desh Ratan Chaudhary,Akhilesh Kumar Sharma

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- A.G.A.
Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J.
1. Heard Sri Pratik Chandra, Advocate for revisionist and learned A.G.A. for State.
2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by the judgments and orders dated 08.05.1990 and 27.09.1991.

The Judicial Magistrate Second (Economic Offences),
Agra vide order dated 08.05.1990 convicted revisionist and sentenced him to undergo six months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs. 1000/- under Section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as ?Act, 1954?).
Thereagainst, revisionist preferred Criminal Appeal No. 69 of 1990 and Appellate Court while dismissing appeal has confirmed the conviction and sentence passed by Trial Court.
Being aggrieved the revisionist preferred present revision.

3. Learned counsel for revisionist contended that punishment of six months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs. 1000/- be reduced and in this regard reliance is placed on Supreme Court's decision in Laskari Ram vs. State of H.P., 2001 SCC (Cri) 111 wherein Supreme Court has reduced the Virendra vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163856905/
1 imprisonment to three months with fine of Rs. 500/- observing that under Act, 1954 minimum sentence is three months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs. 500/-.
4.

entities.text: Laskari Ram vs. State of H.P., 2001 SCC (Cri) 111
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I find that provision of Section 16(1)(a) as amended on 01.01.1976 provides minimum sentence of six months and fine of Rs. 1000/-.

In the present case incident is of 28.12.1977, therefore, amended provision which provides minimum sentence of six months rigorous imprisonment will apply in the present case, which cannot be reduced.

5. No other point has been argued.
6. Dismissed.
Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
7. The accused, Virendra, is on bail.
His bail bonds and surety bonds are cancelled.
The Chief Judicial Magistrate concerned shall cause him to be arrested and lodge in jail to serve out the sentence passed against him.
The compliance shall be prepared within two months.
8. Certify this judgment to the lower Court immediately.

Order Date :- 17.7.2019 AK  Virendra vs State Of U.P. on 17 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163856905/
